item.p: F&O 4.0, fn:civil-timezone (places as IANA zone names, glossary ; FODT0004);
fn:format-dateTime, fn:format-date and fn:format-time, the $place argument (an IANA name or an ISO 3166 country code: the timezone names of [ZN] and the offset used);
the IANA Time Zone Database (tzdata; public domain);
RFC 8536 (TZif), if the data comes from the host.
Unlocks: QT4 olson-timezone 8 (fn-format-dateTime) and the 6 FODT0004 failures (fn-civil-timezone). It also lets users format dates for real places.
Replaces: src/function_library_temporal.c's FODT0004 for every place other than UTC, and the unused $place of src/function_library_format_date.c ('s notes there).

Mechanism: a timezone database (glossary ) answers, for a zone name and an instant, the offset and abbreviation in effect (transitions, then the POSIX TZ rule of the TZif footer for later instants). Country codes map to zones through zone1970.tab. The data is either a compact table generated by a new tools/generate-timezone-table.py from tzdata, or TZif files from the host (option 4: the CLI reads /usr/share/zoneinfo).
Header: none, or processor.h additive (the resource kind TIMEZONE_DATA) with option 4.
Owns: new src/timezone.c, src/timezone_internal.h and src/timezone_table.c (generated); the place hunks of src/function_library_temporal.c, src/function_library_format_date.c and src/format_date.c.
Size: 60–120 KB built in; about 5 KB with option 4.

Gate: all 14 cases. Done 2026-10-19 (), gate met: option 4 (TZif from the host; tzdata 2026e vendored in third_party/tzdata for the drivers and tests, no generated table). fn-civil-timezone 9 of 9, the 8 olson-timezone cases of fn-format-dateTime pass (XQ40 93 of 94 run). sxml-full.wasm +10.7 KB, sxml.wasm +1.9 KB (the places). Not done: a default place in the dynamic context.
